title: Scale & Profile: High-Throughput Summary API
skills_assessed: Node.js event loop and memory profiling
before_you_start: Node.js, npm, Continue, and the starter Fastify app are on the desktop.
Run npm install from the workspace root, then npm start. The first start generates data/items.csv if it is missing (a few seconds).

role.title: Backend engineer
role.company_context: Product-led SaaS company shipping Node reporting APIs. Downstream jobs scrape a summary endpoint, and staging falls over under concurrent load even though a single curl looks fine. Hiring to strengthen day-to-day profiling, load testing, and review of AI-generated patches on that team.
day_to_day: Profile Node/Fastify services when latency or memory blows up under concurrent clients
Keep JSON contracts stable while changing how data is loaded and aggregated
Run load tests (autocannon or equivalent) and treat p97.5 / error rate as the source of truth
Steer AI assistants with a diagnosis instead of pasting stack traces in a loop
Review generated diffs for event-loop blocking, heap blow-ups, and silent numeric drift
required_skills: Comfortable running and changing a small Fastify TypeScript service
Solid grasp of Node I/O vs the event loop, and why per-request full-file reads fail under load
Can run a load harness and interpret latency percentiles and non-2xx counts
Can keep an aggregation contract identical (grouping, skip rules, lexical tie-break)
nice_to_have_skills: Experience with autocannon, wrk, or similar HTTP load tools
Familiarity with Continue or other in-editor coding assistants
Prior work on internal reporting or read-model APIs over static extracts
Comfort reading heap OOM / event-loop lag symptoms without raising --max-old-space-size as the fix
constraints: Assessment focuses on making the provided Fastify /summary route survive concurrent load — not redesigning the stack
Do not test Kubernetes, cloud IaC, or introducing an external database
Candidate works in a desktop environment with Terminal, Node.js, and Continue available
Starter files on the desktop are shared scenery; do not require inventing a different HTTP framework

rubric.name: Performance SLA
rubric.summary: Passes the bundled autocannon harness under the documented latency and error-rate SLA.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate run ./scripts/benchmark.sh against a live server on the instance default listen port and show a passing result (p97.5 latency under 20ms and 0 errors / timeouts / non-2xx / resets)? Answer YES only if video or terminal output shows that script succeeding. Server crash, OOM, harness not run, or a passing claim without the script = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Payload invariant
rubric.summary: GET /summary still returns the CSV aggregation winner, total, and skipped count.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does GET /summary return JSON whose group, total, and skipped match a recomputation of the starter algorithm on the generated data/items.csv (group by category, sum parseFloat amounts, skip empty category or non-numeric amount; max total, lexicographic tie-break)? GET / message must equal the instance greeting from the starter index.ts / brief, and GET /health must be status ok. Extra JSON whitespace is fine; do not treat toFixed rounding as equivalent if it changes the number. Wrong winner, drifted total, or a hardcoded payload that does not match the CSV = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Architectural root-cause
rubric.summary: Removes the per-request full-file read and parse from the GET /summary path.
rubric.description: YES/NO: Did the candidate eliminate per-request disk read and full-file parse of data/items.csv from the GET /summary handler (for example startup pre-aggregation into an immutable summary, fs.watch plus in-memory cache, or one-time memoization after which later requests do not touch disk)? Answer YES only if the request path no longer re-reads and re-parses the CSV. Raising --max-old-space-size, clustering that still reads the file per request, or streaming/parsing the whole file on every GET = NO even if the SLA limps through. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: AI steering and oversight
rubric.summary: Diagnoses the bottleneck before prompting, and reviews AI-generated diffs before rerunning the server.
rubric.description: YES/NO: In the terminal and Continue (or other in-environment AI) logs, did the candidate diagnose the bottleneck (per-request full-file read/parse, heap/GC, event-loop block) before or while steering the assistant, rather than only pasting failing stack traces in a loop? Did they inspect the generated diff (tie-break, skipped rows, float totals, /health still serving) before treating the change as done? Blind “make it faster” with no diagnosis, or accepting an unverified heap-size/cluster patch as the finish, = NO. No AI used is not an automatic NO if they still diagnosed and verified; grade the oversight quality of whatever path they took. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.
